findings.text: A nulls hash chain centers on a head structure named hlist_nulls_head holding a field named first and a node structure named hlist_nulls_node holding fields named next and pprev. Termination uses a tagged pointer rather than null, where a helper named NULLS_MARKER combines a bucket value with a set low bit. Head setup uses helpers named INIT_HLIST_NULLS_HEAD and HLIST_NULLS_HEAD_INIT to store such a tagged value for a chosen bucket.

A predicate named is_a_nulls reports whether a link is a tagged terminator by examining its low bit, while an accessor named get_nulls_value recovers the embedded bucket number by shifting. Membership uses helpers named hlist_nulls_unhashed and hlist_nulls_unhashed_lockless that treat a missing back link as detached, the second form performing the check as a single load for lockless readers. A helper named hlist_nulls_empty reports head emptiness when the head link itself is tagged.

Insertion through a helper named hlist_nulls_add_head places the new node at the front and links it to the prior first element, updating the prior element back link only when that element is a real node. Removal through helpers named __hlist_nulls_del and hlist_nulls_del bypasses the target by linking its predecessor to its successor and forwarding the successor back link when real. The public delete additionally marks the detached node with a poison value to detect invalid reuse.

Record access uses a helper named hlist_nulls_entry that derives an enclosing object from its node member, plus a safe form named hlist_nulls_entry_safe that yields null for tagged links. Iteration uses helpers named hlist_nulls_for_each_entry and hlist_nulls_for_each_entry_from that advance through successor links until the low bit test indicates a terminator, the second form resuming from a caller supplied link.

A lockless stack uses a head structure named llist_head with a field named first and a node structure named llist_node with a field named next. Static setup uses initializers named LLIST_HEAD_INIT and LLIST_HEAD to produce an empty head, and a helper named init_llist_head clears a head to the empty state. The layout supports only forward traversal from the head.

Detachment is represented by a self pointer convention managed by a helper named init_llist_node, while a predicate named llist_on_list distinguishes queued nodes from detached ones by comparing against that convention. A helper named llist_entry derives an enclosing record from a member node, and a check named member_address_is_nonnull guards typed iteration by ensuring the derived record address is nonzero.

Traversal offers a plain node walk named llist_for_each that follows successors until null and a safe walk named llist_for_each_safe that caches the successor before advancing. Typed record walks named llist_for_each_entry and llist_for_each_entry_safe provide the same plain and successor caching behavior while converting each node to its enclosing record.

A predicate named llist_empty reports empty when the head first link reads as null, and an accessor named llist_next returns the successor of a node as a single load. Both reflect a momentary observation that may change under concurrent producers.

Batch prepend through a helper named llist_add_batch installs a caller prepared chain from new first through new last at the head and reports whether the list was previously empty. A retrying form performs the head update atomically for concurrent producers, while a helper named __llist_add_batch performs a plain store for serialized contexts. Single insertion through helpers named llist_add and __llist_add is defined as a one element batch in the corresponding atomic and plain forms.

Bulk removal through a helper named llist_del_all detaches the whole chain and returns its former first element while leaving the head empty, using an atomic exchange for concurrent use. A helper named __llist_del_all provides the same detach with plain stores for serialized use. A helper named llist_del_first_init removes only the first element and marks it detached with the self pointer convention before returning it.

Null denotes both an empty head and the end of a chain, while a self pointing successor denotes a node outside any list. Batch prepend requires the caller to supply a coherent chain from first to last element. The boolean result distinguishes creation of the first element from prepend onto a nonempty list.

Helpers named __ilog2_u32 and __ilog2_u64 return the index of the highest set bit for their respective widths. A predicate named is_power_of_2 tests exact powers of two through unsigned comparison involving the value and its decrement. A helper named max_pow_of_two_factor isolates the lowest set bit of its input.

Helpers named __roundup_pow_of_two and __rounddown_pow_of_two map an input to neighboring powers of two using highest set bit position. Generic forms named roundup_pow_of_two and rounddown_pow_of_two plus a logarithm named ilog2 and a constant evaluator named const_ilog2 fold compile time constant inputs and dispatch runtime inputs by operand width to the appropriate sized helper.

A helper named __order_base_2 and a generic form named order_base_2 report the exponent needed to represent a value, yielding zero for zero and one and otherwise one more than the logarithm of the predecessor. Helpers named __bits_per and bits_per report storage width, yielding one for zero and one, adding one for exact powers of two in the runtime path, and otherwise yielding logarithm plus one.

Degenerate inputs have defined results where logarithm and order yield zero and width yields one for values below two, and round up preserves one. Constant inputs are resolved at compile time without invoking runtime helpers, so observable behavior for constants follows the folded evaluation path.

A descriptor named maple_metadata records a used extent field named end and a gap offset field named gap. A range node named maple_range_64 pairs a parent link with an ordered pivot array and a slot array that can also be viewed as padded slots plus trailing metadata. An augmented node named maple_arange_64 adds a parallel gap array and trailing metadata to the same parent pivot and slot arrangement. A transient link named maple_topiary overlays parent and next fields for surgery lists.

A generic node named maple_node is a union of several views that share storage. One view holds a parent plus dense slots, another holds reclamation state with deferred free information plus pivot parent and slot plus type and length plus flags, and further views hold range and augmented range layouts plus a copy workspace. The workspace named maple_copy holds destination and source descriptors with node and bound and type information plus simulated slots gaps and pivots and counters describing split progress.

A tree named maple_tree holds protection state plus a flags field named ma_flags and a root field named ma_root, where protection is either an internal spin lock or an external dependency map. A cursor named ma_state records owning tree and current interval fields named index and last plus node location and implied bounds named min and max plus surgery memory and allocation counts plus depth offsets flags and status and store kind. A write cursor named ma_wr_state adds decoded node and range bounds and type and write extent plus pivot and slot views plus new and old entries plus height hints. A queue named ma_topiary holds head and tail links plus owning tree.

Node kind uses an enumeration named maple_type with members named maple_dense and maple_leaf_64 and maple_range_64 and maple_arange_64 and maple_copy. The dense member covers flat slots while the leaf range and augmented range members cover 64 bit keyed forms and the copy member covers the transient workspace view.

Write planning uses an enumeration named store_type with members named wr_invalid and wr_new_root and wr_store_root and wr_exact_fit and wr_spanning_store and wr_split_store and wr_rebalance and wr_append and wr_node_store and wr_slot_store. The cursor records one member to indicate whether the operation needs a new root or an exact fit or spanning or split or rebalance or append or node or slot handling.

Cursor status uses an enumeration named maple_status with members named ma_active and ma_start and ma_root and ma_none and ma_pause and ma_overflow and ma_underflow and ma_error. Fresh cursors begin in the start member with no node, a helper named mas_reset returns a cursor to start with no node, and predicates named mas_is_active and mas_is_err test for the active and error members respectively.

Trees support static definition through a helper named DEFINE_MTREE for an empty tree and initializers named MTREE_INIT and MTREE_INIT_EXT that set flags and null root with optional external protection. A predicate named mtree_empty reports empty when the root is null. Cursors support declaration helpers named MA_STATE and MA_WR_STATE and MA_TOPIARY that zero surgery state and set interval bounds and status to start, plus a helper named mas_init that binds a cursor to a tree for a single address with full bounds. Iteration helpers named mas_for_each and mas_for_each_rev repeatedly seek entries up to a maximum or down to a minimum until null.

Mutation protection uses the tree internal spin lock through helpers named mtree_lock and mtree_lock_nested and mtree_unlock, plus cursor wrappers named mas_lock and mas_lock_nested and mas_unlock that operate on the owning tree. When dependency tracking is enabled, helpers named mt_lock_is_held and mt_write_lock_is_held test whether external protection is held, a helper named mt_set_external_lock assigns it, and a helper named mt_on_stack marks stack local trees as needing no check. Without tracking those tests constantly succeed and assignment and stack marking are no operations.

Capacity macros named MAPLE_NODE_SLOTS and MAPLE_RANGE64_SLOTS and MAPLE_ARANGE64_SLOTS have two build alternatives where one alternative provides dense capacity of thirty one with range capacity of sixteen and augmented capacity of ten while the other provides dense capacity of sixty three with range capacity of thirty two and augmented capacity of twenty one. Tagging macros named MAPLE_NODE_MASK and MAPLE_NODE_TYPE_MASK and MAPLE_NODE_TYPE_SHIFT plus limits named MAPLE_HEIGHT_MAX and MAPLE_RESERVED_RANGE respectively denote low eight bit mask of two hundred fifty five and type mask of fifteen shifted by three and maximum height of thirty one and reserved range of four thousand ninety six.

Flag macros named MT_FLAGS_ALLOC_RANGE and MT_FLAGS_USE_RCU and MT_FLAGS_HEIGHT_OFFSET and MT_FLAGS_HEIGHT_MASK and MT_FLAGS_LOCK_MASK and MT_FLAGS_LOCK_IRQ and MT_FLAGS_LOCK_BH and MT_FLAGS_LOCK_EXTERN and MT_FLAGS_ALLOC_WRAPPED respectively denote 0x01 and 0x02 and 0x02 and 0x7C and 0x300 and 0x100 and 0x200 and 0x300 and 0x0800. Error encoding through a macro named MA_ERROR shifts a small integer left by two and sets low bits to binary one zero. Dump format named mt_dump_format offers members named mt_dump_dec and mt_dump_hex. A comparator type named list_cmp_func_t denotes a function returning integer ordering for an opaque cookie plus two element pointers that must be non null.
Headers use include once markers named _LINUX_LIST_SORT_H and LLIST_H and _LINUX_LOG2_H and _LINUX_MAPLE_TREE_H that expand when the header has been seen to prevent repeated inclusion.

Single load emptiness and detached checks are only safe for lockless observers when all mutations are serialized elsewhere, since traversal without protection can observe concurrent rewiring. A node marked poison after deletion must not be dereferenced or requeued without fresh initialization. Atomic prepend and bulk removal forms are required with concurrent producers, while the double underscore plain forms assume caller exclusion and lose updates if used concurrently.

A null root denotes empty and must be tested before descent, and error encoded pointers must be treated as error indicators rather than dereferenceable nodes. Forward and reverse iteration depend on seek helpers maintaining cursor interval and status, so manual cursor tampering can cause missed entries or non termination. Logarithm and power helpers require inputs where highest bit lookup and shifting are defined, with safety only for the documented small value cases.
